visual.general_description: Three-panel figure of an ocular toxoplasmosis lesion: a colour fundus photograph (A), a four-frame grayscale angiographic sequence (B) and a grayscale OCT cross-section (C).

panels.general_description: Row of four grayscale fluorescein angiography frames of the same fundus area, with progressively brighter signal around the optic disc.
panels.detailed_description: Four grayscale angiographic frames side by side, a white letter B printed in the top left corner. In the first frame the retinal vessels are outlined in white against a darker background and a small dark rounded area lies beside the optic disc. In the second frame the vessels remain outlined and the dark rounded area is surrounded by a bright rim. In the third frame a bright hyperfluorescent area surrounds the disc and the dark area. In the fourth frame a large diffuse bright area with a hazy outline surrounds the disc region. A few tiny green marks run along the bottom edge of the second frame and cannot be read. No arrows or readable text are printed.

panels.general_description: Grayscale OCT cross-section of the retina showing layered tissue with an elevated surface and a dark band beneath the retinal layers.
panels.detailed_description: Grayscale cross-sectional OCT scan with a white letter C printed in the top left corner. The retinal layers form a layered band whose surface is raised and irregular on the left, with speckled bright material above the surface. Beneath the retinal layers lies a dark band-shaped area that narrows toward the right, below which is a bright curved line followed by thicker, mottled grey tissue. A vertical dark stripe passes through the left part of the scan. No scale bars, arrows or other text are printed.
